title: autotune: add defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching/caching, new quantization profile management, and unit-economics export tooling. Improves per-token cost by default and adds rollout flags for gradual enablement.
description: Context: This PR implements the first cross-cut change for cost-optimization automation: sensible defaults for batching and KV caching, a pluggable quantization profile registry, and a small unit-economics (uecon) export tool used by the ops dashboards and billing reports. Motivation: many customers are on default configs that are suboptimal for throughput and cost. We want safe defaults that improve median per-token cost without regressing P50 latency, and provide tooling to measure unit economics when we change defaults. This change is tracked in Linear ENG-4872 and PM-1087. Checklist: - [x] Add autotune defaults and config surface - [x] Implement quantization profile registry with fallback rules - [x] Add uecon exporter and CLI for local runs - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Docs and rollout plan - [x] Smoke perf run and canary rollout Summary of changes: - server/runtime/autotune: new autotune manager that loads defaults, exposes per-model overrides, and exposes a configuration endpoint used by the control plane. - server/runtime/cache: tweak default KV cache TTLs and prefix caching thresholds to reduce repeated KV lookups for common prefixes. - server/serving/batching: adjust batching default policy to prefer slightly larger micro-batches for low-latency tails while capping max batching delay to maintain P50. - server/quant: add quantization profile registry (profiles: perf, balanced, cost) and a model-mapping file. Registry supports per-hardware overrides and transparent fallback when a profile is unavailable. - tools/uecon: CLI exporter (uecon export --since ...) that computes per-model per-route token costs, effective amortized GPU utilization, and suggests cost-per-request deltas for proposed defaults. - sdk/python/redwood/optimize.py: expose an API to read autotune state and query recommended profiles for a route (used by console to show expected delta). - docs: ops/autotune.md with rollout steps and rollback instructions. Commits: - "autotune: add manager and config loader" - "autotune: default batching policy and tests" - "quant: profile registry + model mappings" - "kv-cache: lower TTL and add prefix heuristics" - "tools/uecon: initial exporter and CLI" - "sdk: expose autotune read API" - "docs: autotune rollout and examples" Files changed (high level): - server/runtime/autotune/config.go - server/runtime/autotune/manager.go - server/runtime/autotune/defaults.yaml - server/serving/batching/batcher.go - server/serving/batching/policy_test.go - server/cache/kv_cache.go - server/quant/profile_registry.go - tools/uecon/exporter.py - tools/uecon/cli.py - sdk/python/redwood/optimize.py - docs/ops/autotune.md - ci/presubmit.yml - tests/autotune/test_defaults.py - tests/quant/test_registry.py Testing: Unit tests added for manager, batching policy, and quant registry. Integration tests run in CI against a small GPU cluster (presubmit integration) and included a smoke perf check. Initial CI run had a flaky integration test (timeout), rerun passed. Perf: canary runs on internal perf-canary cluster show median cost improvement of ~7% and 99th percentile latency within our SLO (+3ms). Safety and rollout: autotune defaults are behind a feature flag (autotune.enable_defaults) and default to OFF for Dedicated customers for the first 2 weeks after release. We will enable for hosted customers by gradual rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days, monitoring token-level cost, latency SLOs, and error rate. Uecon exporter provides delta projections before enabling. Backwards compatibility: quant registry falls back to previous behavior if no profile is available. No breaking API changes. Migration: a one-time metadata upgrade writes the selected profile into model metadata (fast migration job included as part of the release). Docs: ops/autotune.md contains operational runbook and rollback commands. Known limitations: - The uecon exporter currently assumes homogenous GPU pools for amortization; we'll add heterogeneous handling in follow-up. - Minimal telemetry emitted for per-prefix cache hits; follow-up will add detailed metrics. Rollout plan: - Merge to main once CI green and approvals (this PR) - Bake in main for 24 hours, run migration job on staging - Enable feature flag for 5% hosted traffic and monitor dashboards - Gradually increase as long as cost/latency regressions are within thresholds Review notes: see review_comments below for thread.
